title: Atomic Structure and Amount of Substance
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Chemistry: Atomic Structure and Amount of Substance Worksheets
short_title: atomic structure and amount of substance
standard_text: Atomic structure, electron configurations, mass spectrometry and relative atomic mass, the mole and the Avogadro constant, concentrations of solutions, the ideal gas equation, empirical and molecular formulae, percentage yield, atom economy and titrations.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level chemistry worksheets on atomic structure and the mole: electron configurations, relative atomic mass, moles, concentration, pV = nRT, empirical formulae, yield and titrations. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Change cm³ into dm³ (÷ 1000) and into m³ (÷ 10⁶).
body_html:
How to think about it

The amount of substance in moles is the link between every calculation: n = m/M for solids, n = cV for solutions (V in dm³) and n = pV/RT for gases (p in Pa, V in m³, T in K). Use the balanced equation to change moles of one substance into moles of another.

Electrons fill 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d. Chromium and copper are exceptions (3d⁵4s¹ and 3d¹⁰4s¹), and transition metal ions lose their 4s electrons first.

Example

How many moles in 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH?

V = 0.0250 dm³

n = 0.100 × 0.0250

Answer: 2.50 × 10⁻³ mol

Example

Electron configuration of Fe²⁺?

Fe is [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s²

lose the two 4s electrons

Answer: [Ar] 3d⁶

Common mistakes

  • Leaving volumes in cm³.
  • Removing 3d electrons before 4s when forming ions.
  • Forgetting the mole ratio from the equation.

faq.q: What is the ideal gas equation?
faq.a: pV = nRT, with p in pascals, V in m³, T in kelvin and R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.
